title: A UFO-shaped home for ₹9.5 crore! Scotland's strange tourist attraction has a big surprise
excerpt: Scotland's UFO-shaped Airship 002 holiday home is up for sale for ₹9.5 crore. Discover its futuristic design, coastal location and reported annual revenue of ₹1.27 crore.
content:
Scotland's UFO-shaped Airship 002 holiday home is up for sale for ₹9.5 crore. Discover its futuristic design, coastal location and reported annual revenue of ₹1.27 crore.

1/4

UFO surprise

Ever dreamed of sleeping inside a flying saucer? Scotland's stunning Highlands have a holiday home that looks straight out of a science-fiction movie! Perched near the sea, the futuristic Airship 002 has become a popular getaway for tourists seeking something beyond conventional hotels. It doesn't actually fly, but its unusual design has turned it into a travel attraction. And now, this extraordinary property is up for sale!

2/4

Design mystery

A spaceship hidden in the Scottish countryside? Airship 002 was created in 2016 by architect Roderick James and his wife Amanda Markham as an experimental holiday home. Built using aluminium and featuring distinctive dragonfly-inspired windows, the structure resembles a UFO overlooking the sea. Its unconventional architecture has attracted travellers looking for an unusual stay. But the real surprise lies in how much money this futuristic hideaway generates.

3/4

Crorepati getaway

Can a collection of spaceship-shaped holiday homes generate over ₹1 crore annually? According to the report, three unusual homestays spread across a four-acre property in Scotland generate approximately £100,000, or ₹1.27 crore, in annual revenue. Their coastal location and striking designs have made them attractive to tourists. But despite the reported earnings, the owners are preparing to sell the entire property.

4/4

Price bombshell

Would you spend ₹9.5 crore to own a UFO-shaped holiday retreat? The Scottish property featuring three distinctive homestays is reportedly being offered for £750,000, approximately ₹9.5 crore. Spread across four acres near the sea, the estate combines futuristic architecture with a hospitality business reporting annual revenue of around ₹1.27 crore. But prospective buyers would need to look beyond the eye-catching design and examine what the asking price actually includes.
